sources.title: Glenn Barnich, Friedemann Brandt, and Marc Henneaux, Local BRST cohomology in gauge theories
sources.locator: The full 150-page PDF was fetched and inspected at §2.2 “Gauge theories of the Yang–Mills type” (PDF pp. 5–7), §2.3 “Relevance of BRST cohomology” (PDF pp. 8–13), §2.6/App. 2.A “Gauge-fixing and antighosts” (PDF pp. 14–18), §12.2 “H^{0,n}(s|d): Deformations and BRST-invariant counterterms” (PDF pp. 117–119), and the opening of §12.3 “H^{1,n}(s|d): Anomalies” (PDF pp. 119–120).

contents.name: §2.2 Gauge theories of the Yang–Mills type

source_review.read_extent: The complete section was inspected in the full PDF.
source_review.supports: Defines the Yang–Mills-type local gauge-field and ghost setting used as context for the adopted formal data.
source_review.limitations: The definition separately fixes the selected pure SU(2) model, its regulator, subtraction, QAP input, and continuum boundary.

source_review.read_extent: The complete section was inspected in the full PDF.
source_review.supports: Explains the local BRST cohomology role and the relation of local functional identities to total derivatives.
source_review.limitations: The item states its own finite-jet complex and boundary convention; no classification theorem is imported.

source_review.read_extent: The complete Appendix 2.A was inspected in the full PDF.
source_review.supports: Provides the Yang–Mills BRST gauge-fixing and antighost/auxiliary-field setting used by the worked example.
source_review.limitations: The example expands the local gauge-fixing calculation from its stated signs and pure-SU(2) data.

source_review.read_extent: The complete §12.2 was inspected in the full PDF.
source_review.supports: Identifies ghost-number-zero local cocycles modulo exact terms and total derivatives with counterterm candidates.
source_review.limitations: The authored theorem directly proves its restricted quotient description and does not import the source’s general classification.

source_review.read_extent: The opening of §12.3 was inspected through the local anomaly cohomology interface.
source_review.supports: Identifies ghost-number-one local classes as anomaly obstructions.
source_review.limitations: The theorem assumes an explicit local exactness sequence; it does not claim arbitrary matter is anomaly-free.

searches.outcome: The search did not return the PDF contents headings; opened the known full arXiv PDF directly and inspected its contents page and cited sections.

sources.title: Axel Maas, Quantum Field Theory II: Advanced Quantum Field Theory (full lecture notes, 2024)
sources.locator: The full 188-page notes were fetched and inspected at §4.5 “BRST and asymptotic states” (printed pp. 68–73), §4.7.2 “Slavnov–Taylor identities” (pp. 92–94), §5.2.7 “Gauge-symmetry-breaking regulators” (pp. 120–121), and §5.2.8 “Dimensional regularization” (pp. 121–124).

source_review.read_extent: The complete BRST transformation and gauge-fixing discussion on printed pp. 68–73 was inspected.
source_review.supports: Uses the non-Abelian BRST fields and ghost/auxiliary sector relevant to the local Lorenz-gauge example.
source_review.limitations: The example’s local functional and closure are proved directly from its explicit algebra.

source_review.read_extent: The complete derivation on printed pp. 92–94 was inspected.
source_review.supports: Derives Slavnov–Taylor relations from formal BRST variation in gauge-fixed perturbative theory.
source_review.limitations: It assumes formal measure/BRST variation and does not prove the all-orders QAP or anomaly cancellation.

source_review.read_extent: The complete section on printed pp. 120–121 was inspected.
source_review.supports: Distinguishes gauge-breaking regulators from local restoring counterterms.
source_review.limitations: The definition stipulates its own QAP condition and does not claim a regulator always admits restoration.

source_review.read_extent: The complete section on printed pp. 121–124 was inspected.
source_review.supports: Describes dimensional regularization and pole-subtraction conventions in formal perturbation theory.
source_review.limitations: The definition explicitly avoids a continuum functional-measure claim.
